# OpenWork

OpenWork is the free, open-source alternative to Claude Cowork and Codex: a desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux where AI agents do real work on your own files. It is built on [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), works with any model — 50+ providers, your own API keys, or local models via Ollama — and lets teams share skills and MCP servers. [**Download OpenWork**](https://openworklabs.com/download) · [GitHub releases](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/releases) · [Docs](https://openworklabs.com/docs) Read this in: [简体中文](./translated_readmes/README_ZH.md) · [繁體中文](./translated_readmes/README_ZH_hk.md) · [日本語](./translated_readmes/README_JA.md) Add one OpenWork MCP to Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or another compatible agent and reuse the same skills, MCPs, and connected services across your tools, teammates, and machines. Create something once, share it with coworkers or friends, or keep it for yourself. The desktop app is there when you want a dedicated workspace, but it is not required. You can use OpenWork from the agent you already have. For larger organizations, the admin interface lets you publish capabilities, manage access, and configure shared or per-user connections. ## Why OpenWork instead of Claude Cowork - **Free and open source.** The desktop app is MIT-licensed; no OpenWork account is required to use it locally. - **Any model.** Bring your own API key, sign in with ChatGPT, or run local models through Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server. See [Add a custom LLM](https://openworklabs.com/docs/start-here/connect-your-stack/add-a-custom-llm). - **Runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux** as a desktop app — not a CLI. - **Your files stay local.** Cloud is optional. - **Share skills and MCP servers with your team.** See [Share skills with your team](https://openworklabs.com/docs/start-here/do-work-with-it/share-your-setup) and [Shared MCP connections](https://openworklabs.com/docs/cloud/share-with-your-team/shared-mcp-connections). - **Self-host** the team control plane on your own infrastructure. See [Self-host](https://openworklabs.com/docs/start-here/self-host). - **Bring your Cowork setup.** Skills, Claude-compatible plugins, and MCP servers carry over. See [Migrate from Claude Cowork](https://openworklabs.com/docs/start-here/migrate-from-claude-cowork). ## Install with your AI agent Already use an AI agent? Copy this prompt and paste it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, or any agent that can run commands on your computer. ```text Install OpenWork on my computer, set up my first workspace, and open it ready to use. Follow the steps in https://openworklabs.com/start.md?v=hero ``` 1. Installs OpenWork 2. Creates your workspace 3. Opens it ready to run ## Use OpenWork from any agent The OpenWork MCP brings your assigned skills, plugins, MCP connections, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 capabilities into any compatible agent. It exposes four tools: `search_capabilities` finds what you can use, `execute_capability` runs it, and `list_skills` / `get_skill` list your skills and read one SKILL.md directly. After adding the MCP, your client opens a browser so you can sign in and choose your OpenWork organization. ### Codex ```bash codex mcp add openwork --url https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent ``` ### Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http openwork https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent ``` ### OpenCode Add this to `opencode.json`: ```json { "mcp": { "openwork": { "type": "remote", "enabled": true, "url": "https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent", "oauth": {} } } } ``` ### Any MCP client Use this remote MCP server URL: ```text https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent ``` ## OpenWork Den OpenWork Den is the control plane for managing OpenWork across a team or organization. - Provision inference at scale and control which members and teams can use each model provider. - Invite teammates, create teams, and manage access from one place. - Set desktop policies, restrict local model access, and control which app versions your organization can use. - Publish skills and plugins through marketplaces, then assign them to the organization, a team, or specific people. - Import Agent Plugins or Anthropic-compatible plugins and make their supported skills and remote MCPs available through the OpenWork MCP. ## Licensing This repository uses a directory-split license, similar to GitLab: - **Everything outside `ee/` is MIT** — the desktop app and core platform are open source, free for any use. - **Everything under `ee/` (OpenWork Den — the org control plane) is under the [OpenWork EE License](ee/LICENSE)**, a source-available license. The code is public so you can audit exactly what you deploy. Production use requires an [OpenWork subscription](https://openworklabs.com/pricing), except that it is **free for organizations with up to 5 users**, **free to evaluate for 30 days at any size**, and always free for development and testing. Each `ee/` release additionally converts to MIT two years after publication. Versions released before this license was adopted remain under their original license (FSL-1.1-MIT). See [pricing](https://openworklabs.com/pricing) and the [subscription terms](https://openworklabs.com/terms/subscription). ## Documentation [Read the OpenWork docs.](https://openworklabs.com/docs) ## Getting started (contributors) The fastest path from a fresh clone to a running dev build. ### Prerequisites - **Node 24** — pinned in [`.nvmrc`](./.nvmrc) (`nvm use` picks it up). - **pnpm 11** — pinned in `package.json` (`packageManager`); run `corepack enable` to use the pinned version automatically. Never use npm or yarn. ### First run ```bash git clone https://github.com/different-ai/openwork.git cd openwork corepack enable pnpm install pnpm dev # launches the Electron desktop app with hot reload ``` Coding agents and tests should not open that window on your screen: they use the app in headless Chrome instead (see [Headless web](#headless-web-no-electron) and `AGENTS.md`). ### Repository layout | Path | What lives there | | --- | --- | | `apps/` | the desktop app: React UI (`apps/app`), Electron shell (`apps/desktop`), and `openwork-server` (`apps/server`) (MIT) | | `packages/` | shared core packages (MIT) | | `ee/` | OpenWork Den — the org control plane, MCP gateway, and inference (EE License, see [Licensing](#licensing)) | | `evals/` | executable test specs built on `@openwork/testkit` — see [`evals/README.md`](./evals/README.md) | | `worlds/` | declarative dev/test environment definitions for `pnpm world` | | `docs/` | operator, feature, and release docs | | `.opencode/skills/` | repository agent skills (testing, release, Daytona, and more) | ### Testing All executable coverage lives in `evals/specs/**/*.test.ts`; app-driving journeys use `.e2e.test.ts`. ```bash pnpm --dir evals install --frozen-lockfile # once pnpm evals:pr specs/.test.ts # app-less PR-lane spec pnpm evals:e2e --local # app-driving E2E journey, run locally ``` Runtime-observable changes need test evidence on the PR. `AGENTS.md` and [`evals/README.md`](./evals/README.md) describe the verification contract and vocabulary. ### Sending a pull request 1. Branch from `dev` (the default branch) and open your PR against `dev`. 2. Keep the diff as small as possible, and include or update test evidence for runtime-observable changes. 3. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the licensing terms. By contributing you agree to the DCO, or under `ee/` to the [CLA](./legal/individual-contributor-license-agreement.md); there is nothing separate to sign. ## Local development For one checkout, keep using `pnpm dev`; with no extra environment variables it reuses the existing shared dev profile. To run multiple git worktrees at once, use: ```bash pnpm dev:worktree ``` That sets `OPENWORK_DEV_PROFILE=auto`, derives a stable profile name from the worktree path, lets Electron choose a free CDP port, and asks Vite for a free dev-server port. You can also choose a named profile, for example `OPENWORK_DEV_PROFILE=my-feature OPENWORK_ELECTRON_REMOTE_DEBUG_PORT=0 PORT=0 pnpm dev`. `dev:worktree` also defaults `OPENWORK_ELECTRON_USE_MOCK_KEYCHAIN=1`. A brand-new profile has no stored credentials, so on macOS the real keychain prompts as soon as Chromium persists an authenticated cookie, and that modal blocks Electron's main loop until it is dismissed. Set `OPENWORK_ELECTRON_USE_MOCK_KEYCHAIN=0` if you specifically want the system keychain in an isolated profile. Dev startup prints a banner like `[openwork] dev profile=... cdp=http://127.0.0.1:9823`; use it to find the profile directory and pass the CDP URL to local tooling. If a second instance cannot get the profile lock it now says so and exits, instead of lingering with an open CDP port and no window. ### Headless web (no Electron) To run the OpenWork UI in a browser against a local `openwork-server` (no desktop shell): ```bash pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --browser # also opens it in headless Chrome and prints a cdp address ``` `pnpm dev:headless-web` is a compatibility alias for the same script. The alias remains foreground by default and accepts `--detach`; `world up` is foreground unless `--detach` is explicit. This is an isolated launcher: - Writes `tmp/headless-server.json` and never reads `~/.config/openwork/server.json` - Authorizes the chosen workspace root automatically, and merges (never rewrites) that config on relaunch, so workspaces you add through the UI survive `--replace` - Starts Vite + `openwork-server` with a stable owner bearer forced into the UI. Crash-restarts keep open tabs working. The privileged host token stays on the server process and is never inlined into the Vite bundle. - Proxies Den Cloud calls same-origin: Vite serves `/api/den` (forwarded to the Den control plane) and the app pins its Den API there via `VITE_DEN_API_BASE_URL`, so Cloud calls are never CORS-blocked and stale `localStorage` base URLs are cleared on load - Publishes an owner-only runtime manifest at `tmp/dev-headless-web.json` (`0600`), and allows browser calls to the local server only from the web app's own origins — not every site you visit - Uses stable ports by default (web `5178`, server `8778`; falls back to free ports when taken, override with `OPENWORK_WEB_PORT` / `OPENWORK_PORT`) - Is single-instance as `dev-app-web`; stop it with `pnpm world down dev-app-web` before launching it again - Keeps Vite and the backend under one script lifecycle, so either sibling exiting stops the other instead of leaving an orphan - In detached mode, waits for health, prints non-secret outputs and receipt/log paths, and exits Script-specific options must follow `--`: ```bash pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --replace pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --replace --keep-tokens ``` `--replace` restarts the headless runtime with fresh tokens; add `--keep-tokens` to retain the previous tokens. `--rotate-tokens` is also accepted by this script. OpenWork

OpenWork is the free, open-source alternative to Claude Cowork and Codex: a desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux where AI agents do real work on your own files. It is built on OpenCode, works with any model — 50+ providers, your own API keys, or local models via Ollama — and lets teams share skills and MCP servers.

Download OpenWork · GitHub releases · Docs

Read this in: 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語

Add one OpenWork MCP to Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or another compatible agent and reuse the same skills, MCPs, and connected services across your tools, teammates, and machines. Create something once, share it with coworkers or friends, or keep it for yourself.

The desktop app is there when you want a dedicated workspace, but it is not required. You can use OpenWork from the agent you already have. For larger organizations, the admin interface lets you publish capabilities, manage access, and configure shared or per-user connections.

Why OpenWork instead of Claude Cowork

  • Free and open source. The desktop app is MIT-licensed; no OpenWork account is required to use it locally.
  • Any model. Bring your own API key, sign in with ChatGPT, or run local models through Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server. See Add a custom LLM.
  • Runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux as a desktop app — not a CLI.
  • Your files stay local. Cloud is optional.
  • Share skills and MCP servers with your team. See Share skills with your team and Shared MCP connections.
  • Self-host the team control plane on your own infrastructure. See Self-host.
  • Bring your Cowork setup. Skills, Claude-compatible plugins, and MCP servers carry over. See Migrate from Claude Cowork.

Install with your AI agent

Already use an AI agent? Copy this prompt and paste it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, or any agent that can run commands on your computer.

Install OpenWork on my computer, set up my first workspace, and open it ready to use. Follow the steps in https://openworklabs.com/start.md?v=hero
  1. Installs OpenWork
  2. Creates your workspace
  3. Opens it ready to run

Use OpenWork from any agent

The OpenWork MCP brings your assigned skills, plugins, MCP connections, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 capabilities into any compatible agent.

It exposes four tools: search_capabilities finds what you can use, execute_capability runs it, and list_skills / get_skill list your skills and read one SKILL.md directly. After adding the MCP, your client opens a browser so you can sign in and choose your OpenWork organization.

Codex

codex mcp add openwork --url https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent

Claude Code

claude mcp add --transport http openwork https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent

OpenCode

Add this to opencode.json:

{
  "mcp": {
    "openwork": {
      "type": "remote",
      "enabled": true,
      "url": "https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent",
      "oauth": {}
    }
  }
}

Any MCP client

Use this remote MCP server URL:

https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent

OpenWork Den

OpenWork Den is the control plane for managing OpenWork across a team or organization.

  • Provision inference at scale and control which members and teams can use each model provider.
  • Invite teammates, create teams, and manage access from one place.
  • Set desktop policies, restrict local model access, and control which app versions your organization can use.
  • Publish skills and plugins through marketplaces, then assign them to the organization, a team, or specific people.
  • Import Agent Plugins or Anthropic-compatible plugins and make their supported skills and remote MCPs available through the OpenWork MCP.

Licensing

This repository uses a directory-split license, similar to GitLab:

  • Everything outside ee/ is MIT — the desktop app and core platform are open source, free for any use.
  • Everything under ee/ (OpenWork Den — the org control plane) is under the OpenWork EE License, a source-available license. The code is public so you can audit exactly what you deploy. Production use requires an OpenWork subscription, except that it is free for organizations with up to 5 users, free to evaluate for 30 days at any size, and always free for development and testing. Each ee/ release additionally converts to MIT two years after publication.

Versions released before this license was adopted remain under their original license (FSL-1.1-MIT). See pricing and the subscription terms.

Documentation

Read the OpenWork docs.

Getting started (contributors)

The fastest path from a fresh clone to a running dev build.

Prerequisites

  • Node 24 — pinned in .nvmrc (nvm use picks it up).
  • pnpm 11 — pinned in package.json (packageManager); run corepack enable to use the pinned version automatically. Never use npm or yarn.

First run

git clone https://github.com/different-ai/openwork.git
cd openwork
corepack enable
pnpm install
pnpm dev   # launches the Electron desktop app with hot reload

Coding agents and tests should not open that window on your screen: they use the app in headless Chrome instead (see Headless web and AGENTS.md).

Repository layout

Path What lives there
apps/ the desktop app: React UI (apps/app), Electron shell (apps/desktop), and openwork-server (apps/server) (MIT)
packages/ shared core packages (MIT)
ee/ OpenWork Den — the org control plane, MCP gateway, and inference (EE License, see Licensing)
evals/ executable test specs built on @openwork/testkit — see evals/README.md
worlds/ declarative dev/test environment definitions for pnpm world
docs/ operator, feature, and release docs
.opencode/skills/ repository agent skills (testing, release, Daytona, and more)

Testing

All executable coverage lives in evals/specs/**/*.test.ts; app-driving journeys use .e2e.test.ts.

pnpm --dir evals install --frozen-lockfile   # once
pnpm evals:pr specs/<name>.test.ts           # app-less PR-lane spec
pnpm evals:e2e <name> --local                # app-driving E2E journey, run locally

Runtime-observable changes need test evidence on the PR. AGENTS.md and evals/README.md describe the verification contract and vocabulary.

Sending a pull request

  1. Branch from dev (the default branch) and open your PR against dev.
  2. Keep the diff as small as possible, and include or update test evidence for runtime-observable changes.
  3. Read CONTRIBUTING.md for the licensing terms. By contributing you agree to the DCO, or under ee/ to the CLA; there is nothing separate to sign.

Local development

For one checkout, keep using pnpm dev; with no extra environment variables it reuses the existing shared dev profile.

To run multiple git worktrees at once, use:

pnpm dev:worktree

That sets OPENWORK_DEV_PROFILE=auto, derives a stable profile name from the worktree path, lets Electron choose a free CDP port, and asks Vite for a free dev-server port. You can also choose a named profile, for example OPENWORK_DEV_PROFILE=my-feature OPENWORK_ELECTRON_REMOTE_DEBUG_PORT=0 PORT=0 pnpm dev.

dev:worktree also defaults OPENWORK_ELECTRON_USE_MOCK_KEYCHAIN=1. A brand-new profile has no stored credentials, so on macOS the real keychain prompts as soon as Chromium persists an authenticated cookie, and that modal blocks Electron's main loop until it is dismissed. Set OPENWORK_ELECTRON_USE_MOCK_KEYCHAIN=0 if you specifically want the system keychain in an isolated profile.

Dev startup prints a banner like [openwork] dev profile=... cdp=http://127.0.0.1:9823; use it to find the profile directory and pass the CDP URL to local tooling.

If a second instance cannot get the profile lock it now says so and exits, instead of lingering with an open CDP port and no window.

Headless web (no Electron)

To run the OpenWork UI in a browser against a local openwork-server (no desktop shell):

pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach
pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --browser   # also opens it in headless Chrome and prints a cdp address

pnpm dev:headless-web is a compatibility alias for the same script. The alias remains foreground by default and accepts --detach; world up is foreground unless --detach is explicit.

This is an isolated launcher:

  • Writes tmp/headless-server.json and never reads ~/.config/openwork/server.json
  • Authorizes the chosen workspace root automatically, and merges (never rewrites) that config on relaunch, so workspaces you add through the UI survive --replace
  • Starts Vite + openwork-server with a stable owner bearer forced into the UI. Crash-restarts keep open tabs working. The privileged host token stays on the server process and is never inlined into the Vite bundle.
  • Proxies Den Cloud calls same-origin: Vite serves /api/den (forwarded to the Den control plane) and the app pins its Den API there via VITE_DEN_API_BASE_URL, so Cloud calls are never CORS-blocked and stale localStorage base URLs are cleared on load
  • Publishes an owner-only runtime manifest at tmp/dev-headless-web.json (0600), and allows browser calls to the local server only from the web app's own origins — not every site you visit
  • Uses stable ports by default (web 5178, server 8778; falls back to free ports when taken, override with OPENWORK_WEB_PORT / OPENWORK_PORT)
  • Is single-instance as dev-app-web; stop it with pnpm world down dev-app-web before launching it again
  • Keeps Vite and the backend under one script lifecycle, so either sibling exiting stops the other instead of leaving an orphan
  • In detached mode, waits for health, prints non-secret outputs and receipt/log paths, and exits

Script-specific options must follow --:

pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --replace
pnpm world up dev-app-web --detach -- --replace --keep-tokens

--replace restarts the headless runtime with fresh tokens; add --keep-tokens to retain the previous tokens. --rotate-tokens is also accepted by this script. These are not generic world options.

Open the printed Web URL. Cloud sign-in in headless web uses the copy/paste handoff (hosted Den cannot redirect session grants back to http://127.0.0.1):

  1. Account → Sign in (opens Den; the paste field opens in Settings)
  2. Sign in on Den
  3. Copy the OpenWork link / one-time code Den shows
  4. Paste it under Paste sign-in code → Finish sign-in

Point Den at a local stack with OPENWORK_DEV_DEN_PROXY_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:3005 while pnpm dev:web-local is running. Set OPENWORK_DEV_HEADLESS_WEB_DEN_PROXY=0 to disable the Den wiring.

The other checked-in scripts include worlds/live-app-web.ts and worlds/live-desktop.ts. Both intentionally share installed production state and require their script-specific opt-in after --, for example pnpm world up live-desktop -- --allow-shared-state. List scripts and running receipts with pnpm world list. The headless production world is hard-limited to loopback; remote-access/public-host settings are refused because its browser session uses production credentials.

releases.body:
## Bring Claude conversations into OpenWork

- **Bring your Claude history with you.** Import Claude chats and Claude Code sessions into a workspace from Settings → Import, where they become regular OpenWork chats.
- **Work with connected files on OpenCode v2.** Bring Google Drive, OneDrive, and SharePoint files into your workspace and save edits back; attach workspace files to Gmail drafts and replies, or upload them to Google Drive. OpenWork asks you to approve each transfer.
- **Use computer use on Windows and set it up once.** Windows desktop users can use computer use with apps on This PC. Set it up in Settings → Computer use; chats no longer have a computer status button, and the browser has one button in the side rail.
- **Desktop work keeps its place and gets easier to start.** The window reopens at its previous size and position, Cmd+N (Ctrl+N) starts a session even while you type, and organization switching refreshes your skills, connected apps, and models. Verified sign-in no longer waits for organization discovery to finish. Show model reasoning now starts off; turn it on in Settings → Preferences to see readable reasoning.

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.62
releases.body:
## Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files in OpenWork

- **Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files.** Agents can search, open, edit, and save Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files, including files shared with you, once an admin enables the required permission.
- **Workbot's Browser and Computer views connect again.** If a computer needs an update, Workbot rebuilds it when you open the view; it avoids rebuilding while a task is running.
- **Sign-in and connected admin tools are safer.** The desktop app now blocks unsafe non-web links from remote MCP sign-in requests. For teams connecting OpenWork to other AI tools, Den admin changes require write access, scripts cannot call admin tools, and credential data cannot be read through `den_query`.
- **For admins and self-hosters: Den gets security and recovery fixes.** Self-hosted Den deployments should update for recent Next.js security fixes, and opt-in administrator permission recovery now works with common database encodings. Operators can also enable hashed sign-in session tokens without signing anyone out.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.61...v0

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.61
releases.body:
## Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere

- **Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere.** Desktop users can pop the computer view and floating browser into their own windows above other apps, and browser full screen now fills the display.
- **Dictate messages and use workspace commands again.** On macOS and Windows, dictation shows your words as you speak, stops when you click the mic again, and keeps words across pauses. On OpenCode v2, `/` lists workspace commands and skills, and picking one runs it.
- **Follow Workbot's browser work and longer tasks.** Workbot shows browser activity live and links to pages it opened. Background tasks can pass files and read just the part they need, while longer scripts and documents can finish without a cut-off reply being mistaken for completed work.
- **Invitations and connections take clearer paths.** Invited teammates can join their workspace during sign-in, invitation emails explain who invited them and where to get help, and completed MCP sign-ins no longer appear to fail. Teams messages and Outlook meeting invitations now wait for your confirmation.

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.60
releases.body:
## Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background

- **Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background.** Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also carry less duplicate engine data, and Windows can identify OpenWork's signed app files.
- **Computer use is more capable and predictable.** For Mac users, the agent can script apps directly and keeps working while you use your computer; Take over and Stop return control, and Continue resumes the task. Workbot can also script supported desktop apps. Browser pages keep a steady desktop, tablet, or phone size while the panel changes, and forms take fewer steps. When available, you can dictate into OpenWork or Workbot.
- **Chat can work with more of your existing tasks and connections.** Type `#` to add another task as context, ask the agent to create or move sidebar groups, and find connected actions with everyday wording. You can finish or repair an API-key connection in chat without sharing the key with the agent, and OpenWork Cloud tools work again in older desktop versions.

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.59
releases.body:
## Read, edit, and discuss documents in Workbot

- **Work on documents without leaving Workbot.** When Documents is enabled for your workspace, preview Drive files before choosing Edit when editing is enabled, keep chat open beside a document, and continue your conversation with the file in view. Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides stay in Google and save to the original; on OpenWork Cloud, Office files can use an editor in your own workspace when enabled.
- **AI models and providers work more smoothly across OpenWork.** Desktop users can use existing Azure Foundry and custom OpenAI-compatible providers on OpenCode v2, see organization model changes in the picker when enabled, and find the same available models in Settings and shortcuts. When AI Gateway access is enabled, cloud agents can use supported models assigned by their organization.
- **Admins can check setup before work gets stuck.** Settings › Diagnostics brings desktop startup, AI provider, connector, and deployment-service checks together. Google Workspace settings can also identify APIs an admin needs to turn on, and Workbot explains when an organization needs an AI provider before it can answer.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source desktop hub for managing and sharing AI capabilities via the Model Context Protocol across teams.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenWork acts as a centralized desktop control plane for organizing, managing, and sharing AI capabilities across entire development teams, serving as an open-source alternative to proprietary enterprise tools. It deploys a unified Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that seamlessly connects with diverse AI coding agents like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. This architecture standardizes toolsets across an organization, allowing a developer to create a custom skill or plugin once and instantly propagate it to all team members, regardless of their preferred client. It features OpenWork Den, an administrative interface for provisioning inference access, setting desktop policies, and managing model access securely at scale.
keyFeatures: Cross-agent compatibility: Connects seamlessly with any AI agent or client that natively supports the Model Context Protocol.
Centralized skill sharing: Allows users to configure a custom tool or script once and distribute it across their entire organization instantly.
Administrative control plane: Provides OpenWork Den for managing team access, model inference provisioning, and enforcing security policies.
Unified desktop workspace: Offers a dedicated GUI application to organize connected AI services without digging into terminal configurations.
Cloud service integrations: Natively connects enterprise workflows directly to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 environments.

useCases.title: Standardizing Team Automation
useCases.description: Lead engineers configure a repository of custom MCP tools that the rest of their development team accesses instantly through their preferred agents.

useCases.title: Enterprise Access Control
useCases.description: IT administrators utilize the OpenWork Den dashboard to restrict specific teams' access to sensitive models and deploy uniform desktop policies.

useCases.title: Seamless Agent Switching
useCases.description: Developers working on complex features fluidly switch from terminal agents to IDE-based assistants while retaining access to the exact same custom skills.

useCases.title: Workspace Integration
useCases.description: Teams automate interactions with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace by standardizing those plugins through the unified MCP server.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Development teams, IT administrators, and power users seeking to standardize their AI tooling, manage team access, and distribute MCP skills efficiently. The platform simplifies complex workflows and accelerates development timelines.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: claude mcp add --transport http openwork https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent
